skills.description: Lifecycle email, SMS and push: audits the list and deliverability, then writes the flows this kind of business needs first, loadable as-is in your own tool, plus segments, cadence and this week's broadcasts. Never sends anything. Use when: set up my welcome and abandoned-cart emails; trial onboarding or waitlist launch emails; win back lapsed customers; plan this week's emails and texts; push notifications for my app; why are my emails going to spam; plan our Black Friday email and SMS sends; a send went wrong. Not for cold outreach to prospects — use write-outreach; not the editorial newsletter issue — use make-content; not the whole cross-channel Black Friday plan — use plan-campaign.

skills.name: improve-search-visibility
skills.description: SEO and AI-answer visibility. Use for a site SEO or technical audit with ranked fixes, competitor keyword and topic gaps, a topic cluster, SEO metrics for domains, a programmatic SEO page-set plan, or checking where ChatGPT and Google name the brand. Delivers the requested audit, comparison, map or blueprint with dated evidence and clear data limits. Also covers app store listings and local search. Drafts changes; never edits live. Full pages go to make-content; paid search goes to run-paid-campaigns.

skills.name: make-content
skills.description: Writes marketing content: articles, single posts, newsletters, scripts and repurposed cuts, each with an edit note and a claims check. Use when a marketer says "write a blog post / case study", "write a LinkedIn or X post / thread / X article", "carousel copy", "draft this week's newsletter", "turn this webinar into posts" or "repurpose this", "write a TikTok or YouTube script", "refresh this old post", or "write the page from this SEO brief". Words only; nothing is invented or published. Not for a dated posting calendar — use run-organic-social; not ad copy (make-static-ads) or promo emails (email-lifecycle). Press releases, landing and product pages, and sales decks are not covered.

skills.name: make-static-ads
skills.description: Static image ads for Meta, Instagram, TikTok or LinkedIn: a few truly different concepts, each built on a real ad from the Meta Ad Library, composed, rendered, judged and claim-checked against the brand brain. Use for: new static or image ads ("ten fresh ads this week", "make me some ads", "ads for our sale"); "my ads all look the same"; refreshing fatiguing ads; more like a winning ad; the same image with new text or another font; a rejected image ad to fix; a price or stock change on running ads; a header image or social graphic in the brand's style. Use this, not goose-ads, for any static ad. Not for video (goose-video), product photos (goose-product-photos) or launching (run-paid-campaigns).

skills.name: plan-campaign
skills.description: Campaign planner: turns a product, offer, goal, budget and date into a plan the marketer can approve and a designer can start from today, with every channel kept or dropped for a reason. Zero paid is a valid answer; it never spends. Use when: I have this budget and a launch date — what do I run, where?; plan my launch, drop or Black Friday push; plan a campaign; should we even run ads, and where?; how should I split $5k; plan next month; our CAC blew up — replan. Not for pausing ads on a sold-out product — use run-paid-campaigns; not for an email-only send plan — use email-lifecycle; not for reading this week's numbers — use analyze-performance.

skills.name: research-audience
skills.description: Audience research: who the buyers are, in their own words, where they gather and how to reach them — plus named prospect lists when asked. Use when the marketer says "research our audience", "who should we target", "mine our reviews", "why do people buy us or leave", "where does our audience hang out"; or for lists: "find 50 right-fit leads with emails", "find retailers or accounts to pitch", "score these leads / who do we call first", "who's looking for an alternative to X", "tell me when a past champion changes jobs". Reads the brand's own customer data first and delivers a readable report saved to the brand. Never contacts anyone. Not for market size or trends — use research-market; not for writing the messages — use write-outreach.

skills.name: research-competitors
skills.description: Competitor research: what every main rival is running, launching, charging and saying now, what works for them, and what that means for you. Use when the marketer asks for competitor research or a teardown, "what ads are my competitors running", "how do they price", "find gaps and angles", "what changed this week" (a weekly watch), or "X just launched / shut down / cut prices" (react now). Also builds a sales battlecard, checks a competitor page's tools/pixels, or studies who engages with their LinkedIn posts. Delivers a readable report saved to the brand, so the next run reports what changed. Never copies their words or disparages them. Not for what people say about you or your market — use research-market; not for who your buyers are — use research-audience.

skills.name: research-market
skills.description: Market research and brand watch: which market the brand is in, how big the reachable part is, what's changing, how buyers buy and what they pay, what people are saying now, and what it means for positioning. Use when the marketer asks for market research, "how big is my market", "what's changing in my category", "what do others charge", "what are people saying about us", "is there demand for <idea>", or "watch my brand / tell me if something blows up" (alerts only, risk first). Also writes positioning choices and finished messages ("position my product", "write our positioning"). Researches first, asks only decisions at the end, and saves the output to the brand. Not for who the buyers are and their own words — use research-audience; not for a deep look at rivals — use research-competitors.

skills.name: run-organic-social
skills.description: Runs a brand's organic social: how each platform works now, a strategy per platform and two weeks of posts in the brand's or a person's real voice. Use when a marketer says "run organic social for my brand", "fill my social calendar", "plan two weeks of posts", "grow my X / LinkedIn / Instagram / TikTok", "ghostwrite my founder's posts", "which platforms should we be on?", "plan the social for our launch", "a TikTok or Reel script to shoot on my phone", "tear down @x's account", or "my accounts went quiet". The marketer posts by hand; nothing is posted or scheduled. Not for a standalone post or repurposing one piece — use make-content.

skills.name: run-paid-campaigns
skills.description: Runs the paid leg of an approved plan: checks tracking, pages and stock before money moves, then stages one weekly proposal of kills, scales, pauses, swaps and launches, each with its reason and a check date. Nothing changes without your yes. Use when: launch these ads; it's Monday — kill, scale or pause?; swap this fatiguing ad; we sold out or the sale ended — pause the ads now; an ad got rejected or the account got restricted; we're in a brand crisis — hold the ads; give me the Google, TikTok or LinkedIn changes to make. Not for how the ads did or which ad won — use analyze-performance; not for rewriting a rejected image ad — use make-static-ads.

skills.name: where-to-start
skills.description: First-move advice for an open-ended marketing ask: looks at what GooseWorks already knows and at the site, asks at most five plain questions, names the one thing in the way, and recommends the first one or two moves. Use when the marketer says "help me with marketing", "where do I start", "we need more customers", "sales are flat", "what should I focus on this month", or "I'm back, what's next?". Recommends only; never runs the work. Not for a named job like "make me ads" (go straight to it); not for why this week's numbers moved — use analyze-performance.

skills.name: work-with-creators
skills.description: Real creators and influencers, researched, priced and briefed. Use when the marketer says "find influencers", "which creators are worth paying, at what price?", "find real UGC creators to film for our ads", "who should we seed product to", "is this creator's engagement real", "what should I pay this creator" or "write a creator brief". Free research first; one credit yes only to vet deeper. Drafts only: contacts nobody, agrees nothing, moves no money. Not for AI-made UGC-style video — use goose-video; if unsure, ask: a real person filming, or AI-made?

skills.name: write-outreach
skills.description: Cold outreach a person sends to business buyers: email and LinkedIn sequences, a first line per prospect, reply and objection answers, and a read of replies. Use when the marketer says "write a cold email sequence", "what do I send to this list", "write LinkedIn messages for these leads", "how do I reply to this prospect" or "handle this objection", "reply to this demo request", "win back or reconnect with accounts that churned or went quiet", or "why is nobody replying to my outreach". Drafts only; the marketer sends from their own tool. Not for finding the people — use research-audience; not for emails to subscribers or users, or consumer win-back — use email-lifecycle.
